properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 16 at 7:01PM EST by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
With high pressure building over the region, temperatures will
cool to near to below freezing across many locations. As winds
turn light and skies remain clear, some patchy fog is expected to
develop, particularly around mountain and river valleys. As
temperatures are likely to be near freezing overnight, some of
this may turn into freezing fog. This may even become locally
dense in spots.

If traveling overnight, please ensure to leave plenty of distance
from the vehicle in front of you. Some slick spots are possible
which may lead to unexpected travel issues.

NWSheadline: PATCHY FREEZING FOG POSSIBLE OVERNIGHT

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 16 at 7:59PM AST until November 16 at 10:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Aguada County in Puerto Rico...
Aguadilla County in Puerto Rico...
Camuy County in Puerto Rico...
Isabela County in Puerto Rico...
Moca County in Puerto Rico...
Quebradillas County in Puerto Rico...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 758 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

inches. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.

during this period.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 2:57PM PST until November 16 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves 22 to 28 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach
erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged!.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 16 at 4:49PM CST until November 17 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 AM CST Tuesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 9 feet
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from midnight tonight to
7 PM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 16 at 3:34PM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of storms along coastal and metro Palm Beach County.
Storms may remain pinned over the same area for several hours,
increasing the chances for flash flooding.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Palm Beach County and Metro Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of storms may produce rainfall amounts of 2 to 4
inches  through Thursday afternoon. Higher amounts of 6 to 8
inches with locally isolated amounts up to 10 inches may be
possible. Heavy rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour may
observed with some of these storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Elkhart
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 16 at 12:40PM EST by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart county, IN
EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EDT TUESDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:
Strong northwesterly winds have developed across Shelikof Strait
and the waters around western Kodiak Island. These winds are
resuspending ash from the 1912 Katmai-Novarupta eruption, causing
haze and potentially trace amounts of ash accumulation. Villages
along western Kodiak Island are most likely to be impacted.

Those in sensitive groups or with respiratory ailments are
encouraged to avoid or reduce outdoor activity to avoid inhaling
the ash. The winds should weaken Saturday night.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 16 at 11:27AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory, snow. Additional snow
accumulations up to 5 inches. For the Winter Storm Warning Above 5,
000 feet, heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 2
and 58 inches. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...A portion of central California.

* WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For
the Winter Storm Warning, from 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Monday evening and Tuesday
morning commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

gusting as high as 35 mph.

including Snowman and Dead Horse Summits on highway 89, and Everitt

Weed, and the cities of Mount Shasta City and McCloud.

hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening
commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on tree limbs may
down power lines and could cause sporadic power outages.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

snow expected. Additional snow accumulations up to 6 inches. Wind
gusts as high as 40mph. For the Winter Storm Warning, heavy snow
expected. Total snow accumulations of 1 to 3 feet above 5000 feet,
with up to 4 feet at the highest peaks. Total snow accumulations up
to a foot between 4000 and 5000 feet. Light flurries to a dusting
is possible as low as 3500 feet. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...For the Winter Weather Advisory, Northern Sierra above 6000
feet, including Highway 50, Interstate 80, State Route 4, State
Route 108, Southern Cascades above 6000 feet, including Lassen
National Park. For the Winter Storm Warning, elevations above 4000
feet in the Sierra Nevada and southern Cascades.

* WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, until 10 PM PST this
evening. For the Winter Storm Warning, from 10 PM Tuesday to 4 AM
PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Snow covered roads, travel delays, and chain controls
will continue to be possible through this afternoon and evening
impacting the evening commute. Travel could be very difficult to
impossible Tuesday night through early Friday morning. Gusty winds
could bring down tree branches and significant reductions in
visibilities.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels are around 5000 to 6000 feet
today, with the heaviest snow through this afternoon. Lull in
activity expected on Tuesday, followed by a colder, stronger system
by mid-week. Snow levels 3500-4500 feet Tuesday night, rising to
around 4500-5500 feet Wednesday. Heaviest snow is expected
Wednesday morning into the afternoon, with snowfall rates 1-2+
inches per hour.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Elkhart
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 16 at 12:40PM EST by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart county, IN
EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EDT THURSDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 8:12AM PST until November 16 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
25 to 30 feet. Waves and surf gradually diminish but remain
hazardous through this evening.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and
other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion
may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal
water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
